verticals.label: Private health insurance
verticals.tagline: Dental, vision, private specialist, preventive bundles
verticals.summary: Italian out-of-pocket healthcare spending exceeded €40.6B in 2023 (GIMBE), of which roughly 30% is on dental services. Private dental insurance products for Italian seniors price at €150-500 / year; specialist add-on bundles at €100-450 / year. The largest commercial headroom is in dental coverage and elective specialist consultation, where Sweden's universal-style system has closed the access gap that Italy's private channel could capture.

targets.rationale: 25.4% of the Italian analytical sample, highest income and digital reach (75% internet penetration). Strongest willingness-to-pay signal; primary target for digital-first dental + private specialist bundle.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: 30% conversion × €150-500 / year average dental premium (sourced range from Italian individual private dental insurance market). Lower bound: basic prevention-only product. Upper bound: comprehensive senior dental incl. implants/orthodontics.

targets.rationale: 26.9% of the Italian analytical sample (the largest single cluster), asset-rich (90% home owners). Only 21% dentist uptake vs Traditional Social's 48%. Largest absolute behavioural-gap target if paired with a navigator-mediated channel (e.g. community pharmacy, GP referral).
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: 20% conversion × €150-500 / year. Lower conversion than Connected Active reflects the navigator-channel build cost.

targets.rationale: 7.7% of the Italian analytical sample (smallest cluster) but 48% dentist uptake — the highest of any Italian profile, indicating community-channel receptivity (associations, parishes, broker network). Best fit for traditional broker-channel insurance products.

skip.reason: Lowest income, lowest engagement, lowest willingness-to-pay; falls within public-care perimeter.
Caregiver-mediated decisions; private health insurance penetration here is conditioned on the caregiver, not the senior — different go-to-market channel.

crm_criteria: Used internet in past 7 days (digital reach)
Did NOT visit dentist in last 12 months (acquisition signal)
Reports hopes for the future (engagement signal)
context_notes: Italian total OOP healthcare €40.6B in 2023 (GIMBE). Of which dental ~30% = €8.5B (ANDI).
Italian supplementary health insurance market €6.8B in 2024, +8.4% YoY (Itinerari Previdenziali / ANIA).
25%+ of Italian adults have some form of supplementary health insurance.
Sweden 65+ dentist uptake 84% vs Italy 30% — the gap is the structural opportunity.

verticals.label: Wealth management
verticals.tagline: Hybrid advisor, succession planning, longevity products
verticals.summary: Italian household total net wealth was €11.7T in 2024 (Banca d'Italia); the over-65 segment holds approximately €2.33T of it. Italian wealth management fees range 1.5-3% AUM (AIPB), with private banking at €1.3T+ AUM and growing 8-11% YoY. The differentiator across senior profiles is channel: Connected Active fits digital-native, Moderate Isolated needs hybrid, Traditional Social demands family-mediated.

targets.rationale: Highest mean net wealth and digital reach in the Italian typology (cluster centroid). Best fit for digital-native robo-advisor + private banking hybrid platforms, succession planning tools, longevity-linked products.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: Illustrative B2B sizing: 5% AUM penetration on €30k median investable per individual × 0.5-1.5% all-in fee load (range from fee-only / robo to full-service hybrid), applied to the cluster's projected Istat 2024 reference scale as illustrative scenario, not as a probabilistic generalisation of the descriptive K-means partition.

targets.rationale: Second-highest mean net wealth in the Italian typology, 90% home-ownership, but only 34% internet. Hybrid-channel wealth management with branch + digital-light interface and navigator support is the white-space.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: 4% AUM penetration on €25k median investable × 0.5-1.5% fee, hybrid-channel ramp.

targets.rationale: Third-highest mean net wealth in the Italian typology, concentrated in property and family-decided savings. Traditional broker / family-office channel still dominant. Differentiator: succession + intergenerational planning.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: Higher fee (1-2%) but smaller segment; family-mediated channel.

skip.reason: Median net worth materially below segment average; pension-only living.
Decision capacity reduced by depressive load; risk of mis-selling. Family-only channel mandatory.

crm_criteria: Net worth proxy ≥ €200k (home ownership + financial assets)
Verbal fluency above country median (proxy for cognitive capacity)
Hope for the future = yes (engagement signal)
Internet 7d use AND/OR family member with digital access (channel routing)
context_notes: Italian household net wealth €11.7T in 2024 (Banca d'Italia).
Italian asset management AUM €2.4T in 2024, +8% YoY.
Wealth management fees: 1.5-3% AUM/year (private banking high tier 2-4%); fee-only / robo 0.5-1.2%.

verticals.label: Senior living and home services
verticals.tagline: Independent living residences, home-care subscriptions, age-in-place tech
verticals.summary: Italian RSA monthly costs average €1,700 (range €1,300-2,500); cohousing senior solutions €1,800-3,000; luxury senior living above €3,000. The largest opportunity is the Moderate Isolated profile (26.9% of the Italian analytical sample, asset-rich, socially under-served, 90% home owners), which is the structural target for community-focused independent living that combines a private apartment with a residency-led activity programme and a navigator service — not assisted living.

targets.rationale: Highest fit by far: 90% home-owners with low social network + low digital + adequate health. Selling proposition is community + navigator + maintained autonomy, not assisted living.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: 1% scaled penetration × €1,500-3,000 / month × 12 months. Range covers entry-tier to mid-tier senior-living products.

targets.rationale: Smaller segment but high social-engagement preference. Fit for cohousing, age-friendly community platforms, parish-mediated services.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: 1% scaled penetration × €1,500-3,000 / month × 12 months in cohousing model.

targets.rationale: Premium tier: digitally-managed services (smart home, on-demand companion, telehealth). Smaller share of segment but highest margin.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: Premium subscription €100-300 / month at 5% penetration (smart-home + telehealth + on-demand companion bundle).

skip.reason: Care needs exceed senior-living model; appropriate channel is RSA (residential care) under public-private partnership.
Mental-health support requirements exceed standard senior-living staffing; specialist residential model only.

context_notes: Italian RSA average monthly cost €1,700 in 2024; range €1,300-2,500.
Italian senior-living penetration today is below 1% of over-65 — the structural opportunity is in growing this market, not in displacement.

verticals.label: Pharma and OTC marketing
verticals.tagline: Chronic-care adherence, caregiver-mediated OTC, telehealth-enabled prescription
verticals.summary: Italian pharma spending per over-65 individual averaged €570 / year in 2024 (AIFA OsMed); 97.4% of seniors had at least one prescription, 68% have polypharmacy (5+ drugs). Total private pharma spending €7B in 2024, of which €3.4B OTC. The vertical's targeting differs from financial verticals: Connected Active is a self-care customer; Fragile Depressed is reached through caregivers; Moderate Isolated is the under-served opportunity if combined with community-pharmacy channel.

targets.rationale: Highest chronic load, highest depressive load, caregiver-mediated. OTC, mental-health-adjacent, adherence packaging products. Distribution via family + community pharmacy.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: €60-180 / individual / year on adherence packaging + OTC adjacencies × 100% segment.

targets.rationale: Self-managing customer, digital-native. Telehealth-enabled prescription, longevity products, premium OTC e-commerce.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: €60-180 / individual / year on premium OTC + telehealth subscription × 100% segment.

targets.rationale: Under-served by digital channels; community pharmacy is the natural touch-point. Adherence interventions can leverage the navigator-service investment.
targets.addressable_market_eur_assumption: €60-180 / individual / year on adherence + chronic-care OTC via pharmacy navigator × 100% segment.

skip.reason: Lowest engagement, lowest digital, lowest spending capacity; appropriate channel is public health system.
Healthier than Fragile profiles, smaller segment; not differentiating commercial fit.

crm_criteria: Internet 7d use = no (community-pharmacy channel) OR yes (telehealth channel)
Cohabits with adult child / spouse (caregiver routing)
Specialist contacts ≥ 2 in 12 months (engaged with system)
context_notes: Senior average pharma spending €570 / year (AIFA OsMed 2024).
Italian private pharma market €7B in 2024; OTC component €3.4B.
97.4% of Italian seniors had ≥ 1 prescription in 2024; 68% are on polypharmacy.
